newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian SGB seen buying Tractebel stock from GBL.
newsitem.headline: Belgian SGB seen buying Tractebel stock from GBL.

text.p: Belgian flagship holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) looks set to announce a major reshuffle in the shareholdings of its utility unit Tractebel SA, analysts said on Tuesday.

At a surprise news conference on Tuesday evening Societe Generale could announce it was buying part or all of the Tractebel shares from affiliates of Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL), they said.
The operation could cost up to 50 billion francs ($1.6 billion).
GBL unit Electrafina holds 20.3 percent of Tractebel. Insurance company Royale Belge SA, another GBL affiliate, owns 4.3 percent.
Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd said on September 3 that GBL had offered SGB its Tractebel shares at a price of 14,500 francs per share.
"Frankly, when this report came out, it seemed to me that the deal had already been agreed," one Brussels broker said.
SGB spokesman Guy Dellicour said the news conference was not related to first half results but declined further comment.
Analysts said the GBL-Tractebel scenario also shed new light on a credit line of 15 to 20 billion francs for the already cash-rich SGB negotiated with a group of banks early in July.
"That credit line may be used to fund a larger position in Tractebel. There is a big chance that scenario will proceed," said one analyst.
SGB already has on a cash pile of about 15 billion francs.
One analyst said that if SGB were to buy all the Tractebel shares owned by the GBL group, it would cost about 50 billion francs.
For SGB the acquisition would turn its de facto operational control over Tractebel into full legal control.
Earlier this month Electrafina said in a statement that it had considered whether to sell its Tractebel share, but added that no decision had been made.

Electrafina is also the vehicle through which leading Belgian businessman Baron Albert Frere controls Luxembourg broadcaster Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion SA (CLT), one of the leading players in Europe's television industry.
Frere in the past years has shifted his attention from financial and industrial holdings to the more promising media sector. A Tractebel divestment would free even more cash for CLT, analysts said.
Royale Belge, which had been due to report first-half earnings today, earlier delayed the release by one day.
GBL and Royale Belge officials were not available for comment.
Tractebel rose 125 francs to 14,200 on the news of the SGB press conference. Before the announcement of the SGB news conference, the share had been down at 13,950 francs. ($ = 31.10 Belgian Francs)
